item.title: Matsuyama Castle: Hilltop Original Keep — Guide
item.description: Matsuyama Castle stands on Mount Katsuyama in the very centre of the city, one of just twelve Japanese castles to keep its original Edo-period wooden keep. It is among the finest of them all: a complete hilltop complex of interconnected keeps, turrets and gates, built for defence with clever twisting approaches, and beautifully preserved. A ropeway or chairlift carries you up the hill (or you can walk), and from the top the reward is a magnificent 360-degree panorama over Matsuyama to the islands of the Seto Inland Sea.

item.title: Ehime with Kids: Castle Ropeway, Island Cycling & Ancient Hot Springs
item.description: Ehime is one of the most naturally suited prefectures in Japan for family travel. It offers the kind of experiences that children respond to physically and directly: a hilltop castle reached by aerial ropeway, a cycling route over island bridges with ocean views at every turn, a hot spring town with its own theatrical tram, and a beach-fringed island where the world’s best collection of samurai armor is kept inside an ancient shrine complex.
